item.title: Jiuzhaigou Valley, Aba, Sichuan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
In autumn, Jiuzhaigou Valley transforms into a breathtaking wonderland, where forests burst into vibrant shades of gold, red, and orange, and crystal-clear waters mirror the colorful mountains above. Every valley reveals a picture-perfect landscape, like a scene straight out of a poem or a painting. Located in Jiuzhaigou county, Aba Tibetan and Qiang autonomous prefecture, Sichuan province, this natural paradise brings together stunning alpine lakes, spectacular waterfalls, and lush forests. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site and a China national top-grade tourist attraction, the valley is celebrated for its extraordinary high-altitude waterscapes and dazzling autumn colors. Here, nature reveals both its poetic beauty and its magnificent grandeur. www.chinabound.cn Travel with ease in China, and with meaning.

item.title: 4th Youth Olympic Games opens in Dakar, Senegal
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
4th Youth Olympic Games opens in Dakar, Senegal DAKAR -- The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games (YOG) opened on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic event has been hosted on African soil. The opening ceremony took place at the 55,000-seat Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, a new city located 30 km from Senegal's capital of Dakar. According to the organizing committee, Khady Niang, the ceremonies director, said the show allows Africa to "tell the world who we are, where we come from and where we want to go." Held in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly from Oct 31 to Nov 13, the fourth edition of the YOG will bring together more than 2,600 athletes from over 200 delegations. Twenty-five sports will feature on the official competition program, alongside 10 engagement sports. Meanwhile, Dakar 2026 will also see the Youth Olympic debuts of wushu, baseball5 and skateboarding, as well as the historic first appearance of the Refugee Olympic Team.

item.title: Women, children helped build Terracotta Warriors
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Fingerprint study suggests women, children helped build Terracotta Warriors A recent study of fingerprints is challenging the long-held assumption that the Terracotta Warriors were exclusively constructed using male labor. An analysis of 79 well-preserved fingerprints on the clay figurines suggests quite the opposite. Scientists measured the mean ridge breadth of the fingerprints using a Bayesian model. Unlike many prior studies, this study integrates both mean ridge breadth and ridge density (how many ridges fit in a given space) instead of treating them as independent predictors. The result showed that only 45 percent of the fingerprints were from adult male workers. Nearly 33 percent were from adult females, with roughly 22 percent coming from juveniles who were younger than 15 years old. These findings provide the first quantitative biological evidence for a diverse workforce that included women and children. They may have even taken part in the production, transportation, and assembly of the Terracotta figures. The result was published in the Journal of Cultural Heritage, as co-authored by the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum in Xi'an, Shaanxi province, and the School of Archaeology of Shandong University in Jinan, Shandong province. Of the 79 fingerprints recovered, 73 are surface fingerprints — left by craftspeople pressing directly into the wet clay during modeling and trimming. The remaining six came from the makers gripping small, pre-shaped clay pieces — like armor studs and belts — as they attached them. The fingerprints were mostly found on separate components that had been made in advance, including heads, arms, and armor. The distribution corroborates a production method that is well documented: the parts were shaped in molds and by hand, then assembled one piece at a time. The presence of fingerprints belonging to youths is consistent with historical records of young people assisting master crafters under the Qin apprenticeship system. More proof comes from sporadic textual evidence from Qin legal documents and excavated artifacts. Inscriptions on Qin lacquerware include titles such as da nyuzi, meaning adult woman, xiao nyuzi, meaning young girl, and xiao nanzi, or young boy, indicating that women and children participated in lacquer production under state supervision. "Whether this pattern extended to the massive Terracotta Army production project remains a critical unanswered question, with significant implications for our understanding of Qin labor systems and social organization," said Li Xiaoxi, an archaeologist from the museum who led the research. The Qin household registration system set the age of eligibility for labor and military service at 15. The rules also counted female convicts as labor for earthworks. On top of that, state-run workshops ran apprenticeships where master artisans gave proper training. Together, these rules and practices formed the institutional backdrop enabling women and minors to take part in large construction projects, according to the paper. Proof of women joining large construction in ancient times also appeared in other relics. Bricks on the ancient city wall in Nanjing, built from late Yuan Dynasty (1271-1368) to early Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), were engraved with names commonly associated with females. Leaving one's name was a way to record credit for work. Female bones were also unearthed from a pottery-making workshop in Shaanxi. They are believed to belong to female crafters from the Western Zhou Dynasty (c.11th century-771 BC). "The construction of the Nanjing City Wall and the Ming imperial capital was a state-sponsored undertaking that conscripted millions of laborers from across the country. The population had declined sharply after the wars at the end of the Yuan Dynasty, which made it inevitable that women would supplement the workforce," said Zhao Mengwei, director of the academic study department of the Nanjing City Wall research center. "Scattered clues give us grounds to infer that a considerable number of women took part. They either worked as kiln artisans, taking charge of firing the city bricks, or as labor workers, performing tasks such as clay preparation and earth carrying for brick production. The brick-firing skills could be passed down within families among artisan households, or learned temporarily amid the heavy workload," she said. It is reasonable to surmise that behind the grueling brick-firing and construction work, many more women performed logistical tasks, such as preparing meals for crafters and conscripted laborers. "Though unrecorded in historical texts, their contributions were vital. This shows that cultural heritage is the legacy created by the broad masses of the people," she added.

item.title: Wuxi crowned Jiangsu Football City League champions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
Wuxi crowned Jiangsu Football City League champions Team Wuxi beat Team Changzhou 2-1 in the final of the Jiangsu Football City League, known as Suchao, to claim the championship on Oct 31 at the Nanjing Olympic Sports Center, in front of more than 62,000 spectators. Lu Zeling put Wuxi ahead with a long-range strike in the 29th minute, and Liu Yuhao added a header in the 51st. Guo Jiatai pulled one back for Changzhou in the 83rd minute, but the team could not find an equalizer before the final whistle. Wuxi finished top of the regular season table this year. The team maintained its momentum through the group stage and knockout rounds, and picked up wins over Xuzhou and defending champion Taizhou on the way to the final. The result marks a big step forward for Wuxi after finishing fourth in the first edition of Suchao last year. Launched in 2025, Suchao has become a landmark grassroots football event in China, gathering teams representing all 13 cities in Jiangsu province. Most players compete alongside their regular jobs, making the league a showcase of local pride and community spirit rather than a competition built around substantial club investment. It has also set a benchmark for amateur football events nationwide. Starting from April 11, the league's second season spanned 204 days with 91 matches. It drew big crowds wherever games were played and showed how football can bring people together at the local level.

item.title: German president lauds China's vitality, seeks co-op
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
German president lauds China's vitality, seeks closer cooperation BEIJING -- German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, on a state visit to China from Tuesday to Saturday, hailed China's dynamism in technological innovation, green growth and traditional culture, and called for deeper bilateral engagement. On Tuesday, Steinmeier and his wife, Elke Budenbender, visited the Volkswagen Group China Technology Company in Hefei, capital of East China's Anhui province, where they were briefed on the company's strategy and R&D in China and test-drove a new energy vehicle. The company is Volkswagen's largest R&D center outside Germany. Steinmeier said he was glad to see German and Chinese engineers developing automotive software together, and expressed his hope for closer cooperation between businesses of the two countries.

item.title: Wukang Building charms visitors and residents
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
On a holiday morning, at the intersection of Middle Huaihai Road and Wukang Road in downtown Shanghai, a crowd of over a thousand people at any given moment converges on a single building. These visitors crane their phones upward, frame by frame, to shoot the 102-year-old wedge-shaped facade of Wukang Building, arguably the favorite architecture in Shanghai among visitors from home and abroad. Originally named Normandie Apartments and designed by Hungarian architect Laszlo Hudec in 1924, Shanghai's first veranda-style apartment block looks like a vessel with its "bow" pointing southwest. Renamed the Wukang Building in 1953 after China's liberation in 1949, the eightstory building was home to many film stars and cultural figures in the decades that followed. The building became viral among visitors after it completed a comprehensive renovation as part of the city's efforts to improve the quality of life for residents living in old buildings in 2019. Xuhui district data shows the wider Wukang-Anfu block draws 30,000 visitors on an average day since then, peaking near 100,000 on holidays, with Wukang Building quickly standing as a new landmark of Shanghai tourism. Clarisse Le Guernic, a French woman who has lived in Shanghai for 11 years and now serves as a "Shanghai international tourism ambassador", includes the building on nearly every downtown city walk route. "Foreign friends arriving here don't first look up at the building — they're stunned by the crowd," she said. "They ask: 'Why so many people? In Paris, we photograph the architecture. In China, people prefer photographing themselves with the architecture'." But for residents living in its 114 units, the place is more than a scenic spot to take photos. "For us, this is first of all a place to live," said Bai Zufang, Communist Party of China head of the Wukang residential community. Yet the building's most unusual chapter is not how it handles crowds, but how it managed the first problem its own residents raised. After the 2019 restoration — which took down exterior drying racks and awnings and aligned every air-conditioner unit — the question from residents was simple: "Where do we hang our laundry?" After discussions, the answer ended up on a rooftop platform that was originally the roof of the building's garage. The apartment block was built with a row of automobile garages at its base; the flat garage roof, level with the second floor, forms a wide open terrace that residents can step onto directly from the building. Since this rooftop platform sits directly above the garage, absolutely no drilling into the structure was allowed. To work around this, the heavy planting beds are kept securely in place using repurposed old tires filled with concrete. Rows of bamboo screens were also set up around the area — they gently block the view of residents hanging laundry to dry, while still letting fresh wind flow through the whole space. Carol Richman, a university lecturer from the US, has been inside the building once. "China is filled with wonderful historic buildings, yet this one carries a truly singular legacy all its own," she said. Contact the writers at heqi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Former Kyrgyz PM hails CPC's self-governance practices
item.description:

Former Kyrgyz PM hails CPC's self-governance practices Share - WeChat
Djoomart Otorbaev, former prime minister of Kyrgyzstan, said in a recent interview that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China Central Committee is of great significance. He praised the CPC's continued efforts to strengthen Party discipline, pursue self-reform and adapt to changing circumstances and emerging challenges. Otorbaev said the CPC's approach to self-governance has played a key role in China's development and offers a valuable example for countries across the Global South.
